A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOT/MMA research, with matching authors, equations and experiments. Inspection of all pages, including appendices and rendered figures, supports a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on DOT, MMA and AKI-4B, including benchmark results in Tables 1–2 and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds backbone comparisons, training-length and mask-sparsity ablations, and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The DOT sequence and MMA attention-mask rules remain unchanged: image tokens attend to question tokens during supervised finetuning, while generated responses use causal attention. Additional backbones and partial-mask ablations do not redefine the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining datasets, supervised-finetuning mixture and 12 benchmark evaluations. Blip3-OCR and the AKI-4B study remain in v3's appendices. New analyses reuse existing tasks and data; additional backbones change model configurations rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds Mixed-Attention (MA, Xie et al., 2025) to the central matched comparison, including the retained Phi experiment, and to detailed appendix tables. Its full within-image attention supplies a substantive alternative attention design beyond causal attention and CCA. The separate AKI-4B comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from Phi to LLaMA-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B, with additional Qwen3-1.7B/8B configurations in Appendix E.2. New protocols include DOT finetuning for 10k instead of 5k steps and testing 0%, 10%, 30%, 50% and 100% image-to-text access. The original short-schedule and zero-shot settings remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds longer-training controls for DOT, mask-access sensitivity analysis, linguistic-category attention distributions, and a segmented-region attention case study (Section 4.4; Appendix E.1, E.3–E.4). These examine training-budget effects and MMA's behavior beyond v1's order ablations and qualitative examples, which are retained.

E5.justification: V3 Section 4.1 newly states that results average three random seeds; v1 supplies no corresponding run count. This establishes a reporting change, not an explicit increase in runs. Neither version reports dispersion, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive MA, additional-backbone and ablation results. Retained entries also change: Phi MMA's MMMU score is 37.3 in v1 Table 1 versus 39.4 in v3 Table 2; AKI-4B's reported RealWorldQA score changes from 58.9 to 62.9. Its revised POPE and CV-Bench2D summary scores conflict with retained detailed scores, so these revisions do not establish reliable performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including DOT ordering and the generalized cross-modal mask, retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added; the new mask-size explanation elaborates the existing computational-cost claim.

C1.justification: The central parameter-free MMA contribution remains. V3 adds systematic attention analysis as an explicit contribution and frames the empirical claim across three backbones, reporting +6.2% rather than v1's +7.2% against CCA. The abstract and conclusion omit their earlier no-additional-training-cost claim, although related assertions remain elsewhere.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations linking attention patterns to task-dependent grounding and reliance on parametric knowledge. It replaces v1's explanation that input-order changes may confuse DOT with an explanation emphasizing insufficient training, and interprets mask-access and newer-backbone results. The pretraining information-leakage limitation is retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly documents DOT's approximately four-day pretraining and two-day finetuning durations and describes NLTK-based token grouping and SAM-based region aggregation for new analyses. Most existing hyperparameters, hardware specifications, preprocessing instructions, prompts and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds a focused comparison with Show-o's mixed attention. New citations cover LLaMA, Qwen2.5, NLTK and SAM, and DeepSeek-VL gains a reference despite already appearing as a comparator in v1. The broader positioning around causal attention's cross-modal limitation remains.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized into separate DOT, MMA-comparison and attention-analysis sections. The AKI-4B comparison moves from Section 4.3 to Appendix B, limitations move to Appendix A, and the remaining appendices are substantially reorganized. Main-text framing shifts from the named AKI model toward MMA.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two-column formatting. V1's central comparison table is split and expanded into backbone-grouped Tables 1–2; detailed tables gain MA entries. V3 adds attention distributions, a heatmap, sparsity curves and additional experiment tables, while relocating the existing qualitative figures.

improvement.justification: V1's broad architectural claims relied on one controlled backbone. V3 substantially strengthens their empirical basis through additional backbone comparisons, the MA comparator, and training-length and mask-sparsity controls (Table 2; Appendix E). Attention analyses also make the proposed mechanism more inspectable. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: revised AKI summary scores conflict with detailed tables, Figure 10 contradicts strict monotonicity on POPE, and three-seed means lack dispersion reporting.
